title: Coffee Gift Guide: Gifts Coffee People Actually Use
dek: Skip the novelty mug. These are the upgrades coffee people quietly want, at every budget.
intro: The coffee gifts that stick around are tools that make the daily cup better, not gadgets that end up in a drawer.
Here's what we'd want to unwrap, sorted roughly from stocking stuffer to big-ticket. Check current prices on Amazon, since holiday pricing moves around a lot.
how_we_picked: We picked tools that improve a daily habit across a range of budgets. Specs are from the Amazon listings.

picks.verdict: A coffee scale with a timer. Every serious home brewer wants one and few buy it for themselves.
AeroPress Go: great coffee anywhere, packs in its own mug.
Dripper plus 100 filters, ready to brew.
Cold brew maker that lives in the fridge door.
A vacuum canister to keep their good beans fresh longer.
The kettle every pour-over person has on their wish list.

picks.award: Best gift that changes their coffee
picks.verdict: A real burr grinder. The single biggest upgrade most people haven't made.

bar_tip: Pair any of these with a bag of fresh beans from a local roaster or coffeehouse. Gear plus good coffee makes a gift that actually gets used the next morning.

faq.q: What's the best coffee gift under $50?
faq.a: A scale, an AeroPress, a V60 kit, or a cold brew maker. Check current prices; they move during the holidays.

faq.q: Is a grinder a good gift?
faq.a: It's the best upgrade for most people, but ask quietly first, since some people already own one.
Check the delivery date on the product page before you order; it changes by item and seller.
